interest: Japanese paid press propaganda in France after Manchuria.
overview: This file from State Department Decimal File 894.20251 (Military activities of Japan in France, including espionage and propaganda) contains records from late 1932 and early 1933 concerning Japanese press propaganda and diplomatic initiatives in France. The central document is Despatch No. W.D. 1144 (November 22–23, 1932), comprising a transmittal from the American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim in Paris and a confidential report by Special Assistant Warrington Dawson detailing an instance of paid Japanese propaganda in the French daily L'Écho de Paris regarding Japan's monetary policy, trade surplus, and deflationary discipline. The file also includes State Department Document File Notes (cross-reference sheets) indexing Despatch W.D. 1144 under file 894.51/391 and referencing Telegram No. 15 of January 10, 1933, from Ambassador Walter E. Edge (filed under 893.01 Manchuria/752) regarding the establishment of a central Japanese mission in Paris to seek European recognition and financial assistance for Manchukuo and orchestrate press propaganda.
